# Revali

> Revali is a Dart API framework. It reads the annotations on your classes and methods and generates the HTTP server, a type-safe Dart client, an OpenAPI document and a Dockerfile.

## Revali

Install the framework, configure your app, and run the CLI.

- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/revali): What Revali is, and how annotations become a running server.
- [Installation](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/getting-started/installation): Install the Revali CLI and add it to a Dart project.
- [Create Your First Endpoint](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/getting-started/create-your-first-endpoint): Write a controller and get a route out of it.
- [Run the Server](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/getting-started/run-the-server): `revali dev`, and what it does on the way up.
- [Debug the Server](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/getting-started/debug-server): Attach a debugger and set breakpoints in your handlers.
- [Hot Reload](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/getting-started/hot-reload): Edit a handler and see it live without a restart.
- [Messaging](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/messaging): Consume queue messages with @Consumes, backed by a broker.
- [Testing](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/testing): Drive your server in-process with `revali_test`.
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration): Everything an app can declare, in one place.
- [Create an App](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/create-an-app): Declare the `@App()` that owns host, port and prefix.
- [Configure Dependencies](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/configure-dependencies): Register services once and inject them anywhere.
- [Request-Scoped Dependencies](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/request-scoped-dependencies): One instance per request, disposed when it ends.
- [Flavors](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/flavors): One codebase, several environments.
- [Default Responses](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/default-responses): Set the body Revali returns for 404s and 500s.
- [Environment Variables](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/env-vars): Read configuration from the environment, type-safely.
- [HTTPS in Development](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/https): Serve TLS locally without a proxy in front.
- [Compression](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/compression): Gzip responses for clients that ask for them.
- [Worker Isolates](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/workers): Several isolates on one port, and what they do not share.
- [Graceful Shutdown](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/graceful-shutdown): Finish in-flight requests before the process exits.
- [Health Probes](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/health-probes): Liveness and readiness, and why they are not one check.
- [Request Tracing](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/tracing): Carry a request id and W3C trace context across a hop.
- [Error Responses](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/app-configuration/error-responses): Structured errors that survive a service-to-service call.
- [revali dev](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/dev): Run the server with code generation and hot reload.
- [revali build](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/build): Produce the compiled server for deployment.
- [revali up](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/up): Run every service in the repository at once.
- [revali services](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/services): List the Revali services in this repository.
- [revali compose](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/compose): Generate a docker-compose.yaml for every service.
- [revali routes](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/routes): Print every route the generator found.
- [revali doctor](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/doctor): Check the project for the things that usually go wrong.
- [revali ai](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/cli/ai): Install a Revali reference file for your AI coding assistant.
- [revali.yaml](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/revali-configuration): Enable, disable and configure constructs.
- [Middleware](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/tutorials/middleware): Run code before and after every request.
- [Error Handling](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/tutorials/error-handling): Turn thrown exceptions into the responses you meant.
- [Authentication](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/tutorials/authentication): Guard endpoints and identify the caller.
- [Database Integration](https://docs.revali.dev/revali/tutorials/database-integration): Wire a database in through dependency injection.

## Constructs

The packages that generate your server, client, docs and Dockerfile.

- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs): What a construct is, and which ones ship with Revali.
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server): Create Server-Side Code with Revali Server
- [Installation](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/getting-started/installation): Get up and running with Revali Server in minutes
- [CLI](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/getting-started/cli): Use the Revali Server CLI to accelerate your development workflow
- [Create Your First Endpoint](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/getting-started/create-your-first-endpoint): Build your first API endpoint and see it come to life
- [Run the Server](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/getting-started/run-the-server): Start your development server and see your API come to life
- [Controllers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/core/controllers): Organize your API endpoints with controllers
- [HTTP Methods](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/core/methods): HTTP methods define how your endpoints respond to requests
- [Binding](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/core/binding): Extract data from requests and inject dependencies
- [Implied Binding](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/core/implied_binding): Types that don't need binding annotations
- [Pipes](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/core/pipes): Transform and validate data from requests
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request): The object that represents the incoming HTTP request
- [Body](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/body): The payload of the request from the client
- [Headers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/headers): Headers sent by the client to provide additional information
- [Client IP](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/client-ip): Resolve the client IP from the connection or trusted proxy headers
- [Redirect](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/redirect): Redirecting the client to a different URL
- [HEAD Requests](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/head-requests): A preflight request that return the response headers
- [OPTIONS Requests](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/request/options-requests): A preflight request that return the possible methods
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response): Control the outgoing HTTP response
- [Body](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/body): Set the response payload sent to the client
- [Headers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/headers): Set HTTP headers to send additional information to the client
- [Status Code](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/status-code): Set HTTP status codes to indicate the response status
- [Cookies](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/cookies): Manage cookies for session data and user preferences
- [Public Files](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/public): The directory used to store static files
- [Server-Sent Events](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/server-sent-events): Send real-time updates to clients using Server-Sent Events
- [WebSockets](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/response/websockets): Real-time bidirectional communication between client and server
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/context): The unified context object that provides access to request data, metadata, and more
- [Data Sharing](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/context/data-sharing): Share data between lifecycle components during request processing
- [Meta](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/context/meta): Store and retrieve metadata associated with endpoints and requests
- [Reflect](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/context/reflect): Access metadata on types and their properties using reflection
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components): Reusable classes to handle incoming requests
- [Components](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/components)
- [Observer](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/observer): Observe incoming requests and outgoing responses
- [Throttle](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/kits/throttle): Reject callers that send too many requests
- [Request Wrapper](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/wrapper): Wrap the entire request pipeline in setup and teardown logic
- [Middleware](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/middleware): React to incoming requests by modifying the request context
- [Guards](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/guards): Protect the execution of the endpoint
- [Interceptors](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/interceptors): Manipulate the request & response
- [Combine Components](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/combine-components): Combine multiple Lifecycle Components into a single group
- [Exception Catchers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/exception-catchers)
- [Response Handler](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/lifecycle-components/advanced/response-handler): Customize how the response is sent to the client
- [Allow Origins](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/access-control/allow-origins): Control which origins can access your API resources
- [Expect Headers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/access-control/expect-headers): Require specific headers to be present in requests
- [Prevent Headers](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/access-control/prevent-headers): Block specific headers from being used in requests
- [Pre-flight Requests](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/access-control/pre-flight-requests): Handle OPTIONS and HEAD requests for CORS pre-flight checks
- [Tid Bits](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_server/tidbits): Extra details to help you understand stuff
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client): Create Client-Side Code with Revali Client
- [Installation](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/getting-started/installation): Learn how to install Revali Client and its dependencies
- [Configure](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/getting-started/configure): Learn how to configure Revali Client
- [Storage](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/getting-started/storage): Persist data between client sessions
- [Interceptors](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/getting-started/http-interceptors): Intercept HTTP requests and responses
- [Return Types](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/getting-started/return-types): Support for custom return types
- [Generated Code](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/generated-code): The structure of the generated client code
- [Timeouts & Retries](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/resilience): Give up, try again, and intercept — safely.
- [get_it Integration](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_client/integrations/get_it): Use dependency injection with get_it
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_swagger): Generate OpenAPI documentation from your Revali routes automatically
- [Installation](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_swagger/getting-started/installation): Add revali_swagger to your Revali project
- [Configuration](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_swagger/getting-started/configuration): Configure the API title, version, and description
- [Annotations](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_swagger/annotations): Optional annotations for enriching the generated OpenAPI spec
- [Type Inference](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_swagger/type-inference): How Dart types are converted to JSON Schema in the generated spec
- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_docker): Generate production-ready Dockerfiles for Revali applications
- [Installation](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_docker/installation): Learn how to install Revali Docker and its dependencies
- [Deploying](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_docker/deploy): Deploy your Revali Docker container to production
- [Fly.io](https://docs.revali.dev/constructs/revali_docker/deploy/fly-io): Deploy your Revali application to Fly.io with global edge deployment

## Create Constructs

Write your own code generator against the Revali pipeline.

- [Overview](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs): What a construct can generate, and when to write one.
- [Create Construct Package](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/create-package): Create a new package for your construct
- [Install Dependencies](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/install-dependencies): The dependencies required to create a new construct
- [Create Entrypoint](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/create-entrypoint): The entrypoint to retrieve the code to be generated
- [Construct Config](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/construct-config): The configuration file for your construct
- [Add as Dependency](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/add-as-dependency): Add the construct to your server project
- [Run New Construct](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/getting-started/run-new-construct): Run the new construct to generate the code
- [Construct Lifecycle](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/core/construct-lifecycle): How a construct fits into the Revali code generation process
- [Build Construct](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/core/build-construct): Assets to be generated during the build process
- [Generic Construct](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/core/generic-construct): Non-bundled generated code, assets, or configurations
- [Tips and Tricks](https://docs.revali.dev/create-constructs/tips-and-tricks): Debugging a construct, and the shortcuts worth knowing.
